O.outcome_detail: worksheet production accuracy and error counts

result.effect: 5% error-free; 20% with five or more errors

cells.quote: A study assessing the quality of the production of braille and tactile math and science worksheets (Herzberg & Rosenblum, 2014) found that only 5% of worksheets given to students were totally without error and 20% had five or more errors.
cells.note: The study text reports descriptive worksheet-quality percentages but does not state a treatment-versus-comparison contrast.

D.treatment: one teacher’s descriptions and questions about mathematics graphics
D.comparison: other teachers’ descriptions and questions about mathematics graphics

O.outcome_detail: consistency of graphic descriptions and questioning

cells.quote: Moreover, when 10 teachers of the visually impaired were asked to describe mathematics graphics to BVIs according to the National Council of Accessible Materials’ guidelines, Rosenblum et al. (2020) discovered that there was wide variability in how teachers described the graphics, and in how they questioned students about the graphics features and the information presented.
cells.note: The study reports qualitative variability rather than a conventional treatment-versus-comparison effect; treatment and comparison are therefore represented as differing teachers’ approaches.

O.outcome_detail: standardized mathematics tests across a six-year longitudinal study

cells.quote: Giesen et al. (2012) shed some light on this idea. In a six-year longitudinal study, they discovered that BVIs in schools with more academic supports consistently out-performed on standardized tests for mathematics than those in schools lacking such robust support systems.
cells.note: The text does not report participant age, prior expertise, setting details beyond schools, or a printed effect size.

D.comparison: other auditory forms of the same expressions

cells.quote: The authors found that those who heard expressions using Math Speak performed significantly better than those who heard other auditory forms of the same expression.
cells.note: Participants were graduate students, and none had a visual impairment; the text does not state assignment procedures or the setting.

D.treatment: iPad app for solving pre-algebra word problems

cells.quote: When students used an iPad app to solve pre-algebra word problems (Beal & Rosenblum, 2018), and even performed slightly better with the app than with their traditional methods.
cells.note: The text does not state participant age, prior expertise, assignment, setting, duration, or a printed effect size.

D.treatment: voiced auditory descriptions plus tactile graphics

O.outcome_detail: likelihood of answering mathematics, science, and English assessment items correctly

cells.quote: Preliminary results from a study looking at the effectiveness of auditory image descriptions on math, science, and English language learning assessments for students with print disabilities (Ferrell et al., 2017) showed that braille readers who had access to both the voiced auditory descriptions and tactile graphics increased their likelihood of answering items correctly; braille users who only had access to tactile images actually had a decreased likelihood of finding the right solution.
cells.note: The text does not state participant age, prior expertise, setting, duration, assignment procedures, or a printed effect size.

D.treatment: students who are blind or visually impaired

result.effect: 75% of BVI students are at least one grade behind; 20% are four or more grades behind

cells.quote: Students who are blind or visually impaired (BVIs) are falling behind in mathematics classes (Bell & Silverman, 2019; Cryer et al., 2013), and as they get older, the gap between them and their non-disabled peers progressively widens (Giesen et al., 2012). With regard to achievement, 75% of BVI students are at least one grade behind and 20% are four or more grades behind (Gulley et al., 2017).
cells.note: These are descriptive percentages reported in the review, not effect sizes; the study text does not provide the design or participant characteristics of the source study.
